long_biography.plain_text:
Tabor bought two failing betting shops and retained their Arthur Prince trading name. He expanded the chain to 114 outlets before selling it to Coral in 1995, converting an operating bookmaker into investment capital.

Online wagering later returned to the centre of his portfolio. A founding shareholder in BetVictor, he acquired full ownership in 2014; Michael Barry Tabor remains the company's person with significant control. That status confirms influence or control but reveals neither an ownership percentage nor personal valuation. He has also invested in hotels, property and currency markets, but disclosed company values do not establish his personal wealth. Thoroughbred racing and breeding form a second enduring strand. Tabor first owned horses independently, then built a long-running partnership with John and Susan Magnier and Derrick Smith. Their horses compete under shared ownership, with successful colts also entering breeding structures. Race winnings, horse values, stallion rights, stud farms and partnership entities therefore cannot be assigned wholly to him. His fortune began in retail bookmaking and now spans controlled wagering interests and jointly held racing investments.

The dossier requires the Michael Barry Tabor born in October 1941, British, resident in Monaco, connected to Arthur Prince, BetVictor and longstanding thoroughbred partnerships. A younger yacht-industry executive and other same-name profiles were excluded.

BetVictor's public site does not name its beneficial owner. Current Companies House records list Michael Barry Tabor as the sole person with significant control of BETVICTOR (LBO NO.1) LIMITED through significant influence or control, not a disclosed ownership percentage.

Tabor bought two struggling shops and retained the pre-existing Arthur Prince name. Operator is used because he built and ran the wealth-producing chain but did not originate the first shops or their trading name.

Self-made is supported by Tabor's acquisition and expansion of the principal business. Some secondary accounts describe borrowed acquisition capital and an ordinary upbringing, but the reliable evidence set does not establish his full starting position strongly enough for independent-start or advantaged-start classification.

The reported Arthur Prince sale price indicates a business transaction, not Tabor's present wealth. BetVictor revenue, cash, liabilities, brands, software and operating assets belong to corporate entities and are not assigned to him personally.

Official racing records confirm that many horses are owned in combinations or stated fractions. Horse values, winnings, breeding rights, stallion interests, studs and partnership entities are therefore treated as shared or entity assets unless an individual Tabor stake is documented.

Hotels, property and currency dealing are well-reported interests, but exact current personal stakes are not publicly disclosed. The assets or values of the relevant companies and partnerships are not counted as Tabor's personal property.

The Jockey Club gives 28 October 1941 and East London; Companies House independently confirms October 1941. The date is consistent with the source record's age of 78 on 7 May 2020. Barbados is proposed only as a secondary residence, with Monaco retained as primary.
